passage: Okay, first, I'm Santosh, and I'm no expert. Amma calls me her boy, and this is the boy's story. My friend Gargi told me on a Monday that she felt like a burden, and I said the right things, I think. But my mother says one talk is only the start, so on Tuesday I texted her, "Hey, how's today?" She wrote "okay." The next week I asked her to walk round the lake with me after school. She talked for a bit, then went quiet, and I could see she was still barely eating, still not smiling with her eyes. That's when I understood that checking in alone wasn't enough. I told her I was worried and asked if we could tell her parents together. She cried, but she said yes. Her mother hugged us both. It isn't fixed. But more people are holding it now.

qa.q: Where did Santosh invite Gargi to walk?
qa.a: He asked her to walk round the lake with him after school.

qa.q: Why did Santosh ask Gargi about telling her parents?
qa.a: He was worried because she was still barely eating and not smiling with her eyes, and he understood that checking in alone wasn't enough.

qa.q: What could Santosh add if Gargi's family cannot fully help, and why?
qa.a: He could bring in a school counsellor or another trusted adult, since more trained people can arrange proper help than a friend can.

qa.q: How might Gargi's mother have felt when she was told?
qa.a: She was probably worried and shaken, but also grateful that Gargi and Santosh came to her, since she hugged them both and could now help.

grounding: A teen checks in the next day and the next week, invites his friend for a walk and involves her family when she still struggles.

passage:
I'm Leela, and I share a bench with Manoj, so I saw how it went with Karan.
The day after Karan broke down in the corridor and talked to Manoj for a long time, Manoj walked up to him at break and just asked, “How are you today?” Karan shrugged. Manoj sat with him anyway.
The next week, on Tuesday, Manoj asked again, and on Saturday he got Karan to come for a walk round the lake. I saw them from the bus; Manoj was doing most of the talking.
The week after that, Karan still wasn't eating lunch and had stopped answering questions in class. Manoj went quiet too, thinking. Then one evening I saw him at the school gate with Karan's elder sister, talking seriously. The next day Karan's mother came in to see the class teacher.
I don't know exactly what Manoj was thinking. But he didn't stop after one conversation.

qa.q: Where did Manoj take Karan for a walk?
What might Manoj have been feeling when Karan still wasn't eating lunch?
qa.a: Manoj was probably worried and thoughtful, realising check-ins alone weren't enough.

qa.q: What else could Manoj have added when Karan kept struggling?
qa.a: Telling the class teacher or counsellor directly as well, so school and family could work together quickly.

qa.q: How does Manoj's follow-up look to Leela?
qa.a: Leela sees steady care, not a one-time talk, even without knowing exactly what Manoj was thinking.

grounding: A classmate sees a teen check on a friend the next day and the next week, invite him for a walk, and involve the friend's family when he still seems to struggle.

Friday: After football, Anirban admits to Uday that he has felt empty since his grandfather died, not sleeping, not wanting to see anyone. Uday listens, and that evening tells his own mother, who says to keep checking in and to tell her if things get worse.
Saturday: Uday texts: “Thinking of you. Want to get chai later?” Anirban says maybe next week.
The next Thursday: Uday knocks on Anirban's door and says, “Walk. Twenty minutes, that's all.” They circle the colony park twice. Anirban laughs once, at a stray dog stealing a slipper.
Ten days later: Anirban has skipped school three days that week and barely replies. Uday decides one friend isn't enough. After school he goes to Anirban's house and speaks quietly with Anirban's father on the landing: “He's still struggling. I think he needs more than me.” That evening Anirban's father calls the school counsellor to set up a meeting.

qa.q: What made Anirban laugh during the walk?
qa.a: A stray dog stealing a slipper.

qa.q: Why did Uday decide one friend wasn't enough?
qa.a: Uday grew worried when Anirban kept skipping school and barely replied, sensing the sadness went deeper than a friend could handle.

qa.q: What else could Uday keep doing after involving the family?
qa.a: Keep the short walks and chai invites going, so Anirban still has a friend alongside the adults' help.

qa.q: How might Anirban's father see Uday's visit?
qa.a: Anirban's father would likely be grateful and concerned, and he acted that evening by calling the counsellor.
